cultural.vision_reason: The image shows a carved wooden mother-and-child figure with bead adornment, identified as Pende-style Central African sculpture. It fits the claimed Pende ethnicity and category.

physical.title: Mother-and-Child Figure
physical.medium_raw: Wood, glass beads, upholstery studs, natural fiber, and pigment
physical.summary: Wearing an elaborate lobed headdress and a beaded waistbelt, and having filed teeth and red-powdered skin, this maternity figure seems to have once carried an ax and a cup, wooden imitations of the two most important chiefly attributes. Perhaps together with a male counterpart, it was secretly kept inside the ritual house, serving as a guardian of the chief’s treasure. Its style places it in the westernmost corner of Pendeland, between the Lutshima and Kwilu rivers.

location.made_in_place: Africa, Central Africa, Democratic Republic of Congo, Pende-style maker
